items.title: Randomized procedures as probability kernels
items.statement: For a statistical experiment with data measurable space (X,A) and an action measurable space (D,G), a randomized procedure is a probability kernel K from (X,A) to (D,G): for every x, K(x,.) is a probability measure on (D,G), and for every B in G, x maps to K(x,B) is A-measurable. K(x,B) is the probability of an action in B after observing x; K does not depend on the unknown parameter.

references.title: Ryan Martin, Lecture Notes on Advanced Statistical Theory, §5.1, PDF pp. 100–102
Peter Hoff, Statistical Decision Problems, §§2–4.2, PDF pp. 2–8
Peter Kempthorne, MIT 18.655 Lecture Note 6: Sufficiency, PDF pp. 14–15

items.title: A randomized procedure has a measurable action law
items.statement: Let K be a randomized procedure for an experiment ((X,A),Theta,(P_theta)) with action space (D,G). Give [0,infinity] its Borel sigma-algebra. For every nonnegative G/B([0,infinity])-measurable g:D->[0,infinity], x maps to integral g(a) K(x,da) is A-measurable. For each theta, Q_theta(B)=integral K(x,B) P_theta(dx) is a probability measure on (D,G), and integral g dQ_theta equals integral [integral g(a)K(x,da)] P_theta(dx), with extended nonnegative values allowed.
items.strategy: Use increasing simple approximations and pointwise monotone convergence to prove measurability of integration against the supplied kernel. Normalize the action law, prove countable additivity by monotone convergence of finite event sums, establish the iterated-integral identity for indicators and simple functions, then pass to all nonnegative measurable functions by monotone convergence.

references.title: Ryan Martin, Lecture Notes on Advanced Statistical Theory, §5.1, PDF pp. 100–102
Peter Hoff, Statistical Decision Problems, §§2–4.2, PDF pp. 2–8

items.title: Statistics and estimators
items.statement: In a statistical experiment with data measurable space (X,A), a statistic with target measurable space (Y,B) is an A/B-measurable map T:X→Y. For an estimand psi:Theta→Y whose target set Y is equipped with B, an estimator of psi is a statistic with that same target space; its value at x is an estimate. The parameter map psi need not be measurable, since the experiment imposes no measurable structure on Theta.

references.title: Ryan Martin, Lecture Notes on Advanced Statistical Theory, §5.1, PDF pp. 100–102
Peter Hoff, Statistical Decision Problems, §2, PDF pp. 2–3

items.title: Randomized tests
items.statement: A randomized test is a randomized procedure with binary action space ({0,1},2^{ {0,1} }), where 1 means reject and 0 means do not reject. Its test function is phi(x)=K(x,{1}), a measurable map X→[0,1]; phi(x) is the probability of rejection conditional on observed data x, and 1-phi(x) is the probability of no rejection.

references.title: Ryan Martin, Lecture Notes on Advanced Statistical Theory, §5.1, PDF pp. 100–102
Peter Hoff, Statistical Decision Problems, §3, PDF pp. 4–5

items.title: A deterministic statistic is a Dirac kernel
items.statement: Let T:(X,A)->(Y,B) be a statistic in a statistical experiment. The procedure K(x,C)=delta_{T(x)}(C)=1_C(T(x)) is a probability kernel and always takes the action T(x).
items.strategy: Verify pointwise that the Dirac section is a probability measure. For each measurable action event, its kernel evaluation is the indicator of the measurable preimage under T.

items.title: A coin-flip randomized test
items.statement: On the one-point data space {x0}, let the experiment have one parameter theta and sampling law delta_{x0}. For any p in [0,1], the binary procedure K(x0,{1})=p and K(x0,{0})=1-p is a randomized test whose rejection probability is p.
items.strategy: Check the four binary action events to verify a probability measure and the one-point kernel measurability condition. Integrate the rejection evaluation under the point-mass data law to obtain p, including p=0 and p=1.

items.title: A nonmeasurable rule is not a statistic or test
items.statement: The claim that every set map from a statistical data space to the binary action space is a statistic or a randomized test function is false. Let X={0,1} carry the trivial sigma-algebra and let phi(x)=x into {0,1} with its full sigma-algebra. Then phi is not measurable.
items.strategy: Construct a one-parameter experiment on the trivial sigma-algebra, then show the preimage of the measurable rejection event {1} is not measurable. Apply the statistic and test definitions to refute the claim.
